To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dietary restriction of 30-40% suppresses mammary expression of mouse mammary tumor proviral RNA in C3H/Oue mice, and that this suppression is independent of pregnancy, lactation, prolactin, or any other known hormonal factor.
dietary restriction prevents mammary tumor induction in C3H/OU mice by suppressing mammary MMT expression and that dietary restriction permits normal gestation and lactations in C3H/OU mice.

dietary restriction of C57BL/6 and C3H/Ov mice prevents the spontaneous development of mammary tumors by suppressing mouse mammary tumor proviral transcription, and permits normal conception, pregnancy, lactation and the production of normal litters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of dietary restriction on MMTV expression, mammary tumorigenesis, and mammary gland involution.
the influence of chronic energy intake restriction (CEIR) on spontaneous mammary tumor development and the mechanism of this effect.
the effects of chronic energy intake restriction (CEIR) on the incidence of mammary adenocarciomata in C3H/Ouj mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

dietary restriction suppresses MMTV transcription even after mammosomatotropic hormone levels are high and mammary glands are undergoing involution, and that the suppression is independent of prolactin levels.
dietary restriction is an effective method of preventing mammary tumor development, and that it does not adversely affect fertility or the production of healthy offspring.
dietary restriction is a highly effective and specific means of suppressing MMTV transcription, and that this suppression is not dependent on the nutritional demands of lactation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary restriction suppresses mammary tumor development by suppressing MMTV transcription in the mammary gland, and that this suppression is not due to a reduction of serum prolactin.
dietary energy restriction suppresses MMTV transcription in the mammary gland of C3H mice, and prevents the development of mammary tumors, even after involution.
the suppression of mammary MMTv mRNA expression in CEIR mice may be mediated by prolactin and/or other factors, but that the mechanism is independent of energy restriction per se.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary restriction is an effective means to prevent mammary tumor development and that the dietary restriction of C57BL/6 mice is an effective means for the prevention of mammary tumorigenesis.
dietary restriction is not a starvation diet.

the level of mammary MMTVs transcription is rigorously controlled by the level of dietary restriction, even when dietary restriction is interrupted by periods of ad libitium consumption, as occurs during mating, gestation, and lactation.
